name: The Old Bazaar and Castle Quarter
tagline: Kruja's historic heart, wooden shops and Skanderbeg's fortress
description: The steep cobbled lane of the Ottoman-era bazaar climbs toward Skanderbeg's castle, lined with wooden shops selling carpets, antiques, and crafts, plus the Skanderbeg Museum and Ethnographic Museum. This is where nearly all visitor activity concentrates, from morning until early evening. Cafes here offer the best (if still modest) wifi in town.

name: Lower Kruja (New Town)
tagline: The modern residential center below the old bazaar
description: Downhill from the castle quarter, this is where most residents actually live, with everyday shops, schools, the main square, and more affordable, informal apartment rentals. It lacks the postcard charm of the bazaar but offers flatter streets, better car access, and a more local, less touristic pace of life.
bestFor: longer stays, budget renters, quieter living
pros: Cheaper rentals than the old town

name: The Tirana Road Corridor
tagline: The route linking Kruja to the capital and the airport
description: The road descending from Kruja toward the SH2 highway and on to Tirana and Rinas Airport is where furgon minibuses and taxis run daily. A few roadside guesthouses, petrol stations, and small businesses sit along this stretch, useful for anyone prioritizing easy transit connections over proximity to the bazaar's charm.
pros: Fast access to Tirana and the airport
cons: Further from the bazaar and castle

name: Sari Salltik and the Mountain Slopes
tagline: The wooded hillside above Kruja with sweeping views
description: Above the castle, trails climb toward the Sari Salltik shrine and the forested slopes of Mount Kruja, offering panoramic views over the town, the Tirana plain, and the Adriatic coast on clear days. A quiet, largely undeveloped area favored for short hikes and picnics rather than accommodation.
pros: Best panoramic views in the area
